In other than Celtic countries surnames have most frequently originated from nicknames descriptive of the personal peculiarities of some early ancestor. Thus in England we find families bearing such names as White, Black, Short, Long, etc. ;

It is certainly not the fact that descriptive nicknames were uncommon amongst the Celts. On the contrary, the quick fancy of this race has always displayed itself in the readiness with which sobriquets of this kind were invented.
